resale_co.name: Resale inspection (Residential Resale / Rental Inspection)
resale_co.issued_by: Construction & Code Enforcement (Code Enforcement / Housing Official)
resale_co.lead_time: Inspections are done on Fridays only
requirements: Yard free of debris and weeds and sheds empty; waterfront lots: bulkhead in good condition, fill maintained on the landward side, no floatable debris around or under the house
Home clean and move-in ready: trash, debris and hazardous material removed; paint, flooring, siding, roofing, windows and screens in good condition

Attached garage: 1/2 inch drywall on walls next to living space and on attic ceilings; two layers of type X drywall under living space above the garage; metal or rated doors in separation walls, including attic access
Stairs with graspable handrails and closed risers; decks and landings 30 inches or more above grade need 36 inch guardrails with openings under 4 inches
Smoke detectors to code (at least one per floor level in older homes and one within 10 feet of each bedroom) and CO detector within 10 feet of all bedrooms
Anti-tip device on the range
Electrical: no exposed wires, panel labeled, all boxes covered
Plumbing: water heater relief valve piped to within 6 inches of the floor; heating equipment properly vented
House numbers at least 4 inches near the front door (not on the door) and contrasting
Chimney caps on all fireplaces
For resales: well water test by the Board of Health (if on a well), Elevation Certificate and Septic Certificate (checklist marks these 'For resales and rentals')
Bulkhead certificate if the bulkhead is in questionable repair (decided the day of inspection)
Portable fire extinguisher, minimum 2A:10B:C, 2 1/2 to 10 lb dry chemical, within 10 feet of the kitchen (form still lists it)
No sleeping space on the third floor in Tuckerton Meadows or in second-floor loft areas in Bartletts Landing
Owner signs that all checklist items were checked
resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Borough's Rental/Resale Application packet (fillable PDF, updated 10/2026; check 'Resale Inspection', give closing date and access or lock box instructions), attach the required professional certifications, and submit it to Construction & Code Enforcement, 420 East Main Street (609-296-4916, Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 3:30 pm). Cash, check or money order only. Inspections are Fridays only.

evidence.quote: Attach all Required Certifications: Well & Septic (Well Water Test must be completed by the Board of Health),
Water test required for well water by Board of Health.
to be determined the day of inspection
Building, Zoning & Code Enforcement Telephone: 609-296-4916 Or 609-296-2447

resale_co.notes: The Forms page now links a new typed, fillable 'Rental & Resale Inspection Checklist' packet (UPDATED 10/2026; PDF created October 13, 2026) in place of the May 2026 scan. It still has four pages: the fire certificate application (page 1), the smoke/CO requirements (page 2), the resale or rental inspection application (page 3) and Code Enforcement's 21-item 'Residential Resale / Rental Inspection Checklist' (page 4), so a housing inspection on resale is part of the process. What changed: the checklist now marks which certificates apply. Chimney, woodstove, fireplace, heat and hot water and lead paint certificates are 'For rentals only'; the well water test, Elevation Certificate and Septic Certificate are 'For resales and rentals'; the bulkhead certificate is only needed if the bulkhead looks to be in questionable repair. Page 3 still asks to attach all certifications in one line, so confirm which ones a resale really needs. A $50.00 re-inspection fee is now printed (see fire certificate). The ordinance itself was not viewed (ecode360). The packet does not show a separate fee for the resale housing checklist. The Borough web page links Joe Ventresca's name to the Technical Assistant's address (LCranmer@TuckertonBorough.com, Lindsay Cranmer), so no personal email is listed for him. Other contacts: Code Enforcement Officer and Deputy Zoning Officer James McAndrew (JMCANDREW@TuckertonBorough.com, 609-296-3254).

requirements: Smoke detectors on each level and outside each sleeping area near the bedrooms; hardwired or interconnected alarms required by year built: 1979 to 1981 hardwired outside sleeping areas; 1981 to 1987 hardwired outside sleeping areas and in the basement; 1987 to 1991 hardwired interconnected on each level; 1991 to present hardwired interconnected with battery backup in all bedrooms, outside each sleeping area and on every level

Since January 1, 2019 battery smoke alarms must be 10-year sealed units; all non-sealed battery detectors must be replaced; hardwired alarms from original construction may not be replaced with battery alarms
Smoke detectors not within 3 feet of a kitchen or bathroom, not within 20 feet of a flame-producing device, and not within 4 inches of a corner or lower than 12 inches from the ceiling on a wall
CO alarm within 10 feet of the sleeping areas
Portable fire extinguisher still on the October 2026 Borough form: minimum 2A:10B:C, 2 1/2 to 10 lb dry chemical, within 10 feet of the kitchen
If detectors cannot be reached, provide a ladder or a notarized letter stating they are in good working condition

authorities.name: Borough of Tuckerton Fire Prevention (Construction & Code Enforcement office)
authorities.lead_time: Apply more than 10 business days ahead for the lowest fee; inspections Fridays only; must be done before the new owners occupy

fees.label: Inspection done more than 10 business days after the application is received
fees.quote: $75.00 - Inspection will be done more than 10 business days after the application is received.

fees.label: Inspection done 4 to 10 business days after the application is received
fees.quote: $150.00 - Inspection will be done 4 to 10 business days after the application is received.

fees.label: Inspection done 1 to 4 business days after the application is received
fees.quote: $225.00 - Inspection will be done 1 to 4 business days after the application is received.

fees.label: Re-inspection after a failed inspection
fees.quote: There is a $50.00 re-inspection fee if the inspection is failed.

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out page 1 of the Borough's Rental/Resale Application (fillable PDF, updated 10/2026: inspection address, owners, buyers, contact person, closing date) and bring it with the non-refundable fee to 420 East Main Street, Tuckerton (609-296-4916). Cash, check or money order only. Inspections are Fridays only. A failed inspection costs $50.00 to re-inspect.
authorities.contact_title: Construction Official, Zoning Official, Fire Protection Subcode Official and Fire Protection Inspector

evidence.quote: Certification of smoke detector, carbon monoxide alarm and portable fire extinguisher compliance
Upon the change of ownership (resale) of any real property, a Fire Certificate must be applied for, for the inspection of Smoke Detectors, Carbon Monoxide Detectors and Fire Extinguishers only.
This inspection must be done prior to the new owners occupying said dwelling.
WE ONLY ACCEPT CASH, CHECK, OR MONEY ORDER
please provide a ladder or a notarized letter stating they are in good working condition.

fire_cert.notes: The July 2026 LEA registry lists the NJ DCA Division of Fire Safety (S) as Tuckerton's fire code enforcing agency, but the DCA's list of state-enforced towns (revised 7/17/2026) shows 'TUCKERTON 1532' without the 'SC' (smoke certs) mark, and the Borough's own 2026 Rental/Resale packet has the Borough's Fire Prevention office issue the smoke/CO certificate. So sellers use the Borough, not the DCA online portal. Tuckerton has no separate page in the state fire directory. The Borough's fees ($75 / $150 / $225) are higher than the state DCA schedule. The October 2026 form adds a $50.00 re-inspection fee for a failed inspection; the $75 / $150 / $225 tiers did not change. The form still requires a fire extinguisher although P.L.2025, c.19 removed it from the state requirement; it also does not mention the new secondary power source label.

other_items.label: Professional certifications for resales
other_items.detail: The October 2026 checklist lists a well water test by the Board of Health (if on a well), an Elevation Certificate and a Septic Certificate for resales and rentals. Chimney, woodstove, fireplace, heat and hot water and lead paint certificates are now marked for rentals only.

other_items.label: Bulkhead certificate (waterfront)
other_items.detail: Needed only if the bulkhead is in questionable repair, decided on the day of inspection.
